minutes.headline: Committee approved posting psychologist and social worker jobs and heard a primary fire alarm upgrade quote.
minutes.summary: The remote School Committee approved a small line-item transfer and permission to post a full-time psychologist and two grant-funded social worker positions. It heard the facilities director's quote to replace the primary school fire alarm, a superintendent's report, and a long progress report on the improvement strategy. It then went into executive session on union negotiations, not to return.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted 5-0 to allow posting of a full-time psychologist and two grant-funded social worker positions.
The committee voted 5-0 on a small line-item transfer from unemployment compensation to collaborative tuitions, for added out-of-district services.
The facilities director presented a quote to replace the primary school fire alarm; a state earmark covers part of it and the rest is unfunded.
The MyCAP presentation was moved to the next meeting, and the combined staff appreciation resolution was signed.
After a long improvement-strategy progress report, the committee went into executive session on union negotiations and did not return.

why_it_matters: The fire alarm cost not covered by the state earmark would have to come from capital planning or end-of-year school surplus, so it may reach residents as a capital request.
The social worker posts are meant to be paid from temporary grants rather than the local budget, so those jobs depend on grant money that is not permanent.
